pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Visibilty Inheritance, universal ComputedVisibility and RenderLayers support
pr_comments: Does this supercede #5089? I don't *think* this will fix #5183; do you want to toss that in?

This fixes #5089. It does not add "renderlayer visibility inheritance", so it does not fix #5183. If we choose to support that (and it seems like we might want to), I think we should probably do that in a separate PR.
My apologies, I meant to ask if this supercedes #5114.

> My apologies, I meant to ask if this supercedes #5114.

Yes.

Hmm some thoughts on "light renderlayers":
* Lights are both "visible" to cameras and "see" entities. Naively, porting them to RenderLayers means that value means "both" things. I think this means we need to split out RenderLayers from VisibleRenderLayers. Cameras only "see" things, so they have VisibleRenderLayers. Lights are both "seen" and "see things" so they have both.
*  We should really split out VisibleEntities from VisibleLights (and maybe even finer granularity) for performance reasons. No sense in iterating over a list that contains both across both contexts. This would require some changes to `check_visibility`.
* This adds enough complexity that it probably deserves a follow up. The current behavior in the PR appears to be equivalent to `main`.

I did get "per view directional lights using render layers" working though, but I don't think I will push those changes here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2694663/178847086-1a7d32a3-cf70-41f9-9ade-48579ddf8667.png)
Alrighty I think this is in a good spot now!

review_comments: Why the difference here? Point lights above use `is_visible_in_hierarchy()`. Off the top of my head reading this I'm not sure if light view visibility has been done yet here.

I think both should be is_visible() as that means they are both visible in hierarchical terms, and visible in at least one view, which means that their bounds intersect at least one view so they can impact how it looks/they look.
Ah yeah the above should also be `is_visible`
This PR shows a lot of duplication in Bundle structs. It might be worth considering a macro or some other way to compose bundles.
Yeah; we should consider using nested bundles here in the future.

Yeah finding a way to compose bundles is worth considering. We already have "bundle nesting" but I don't like the ux of that on the user side (flat lists of components are way easier to work with and understand). Open to exploring things that improve on this, ideally while keeping flat lists (or at least, no arbitrary levels of bundle nesting).

It would be nice if there were a way to expand a bundle into another bundle, so you could do something like:
```rust
(
    ..BundleA {},
    ..BundleB {},
)
```
You'd have to handle situations where there are common components though.

Why explicitly this is after CheckVisibility but not update_point_light_frusta nor update_spot_light_frusta? Because they are after AssignLightsToClusters which itself is after CheckVisibility? This is a case where I prefer explicit dependencies I think as things get changed and implicit dependency ordering will catch us out. Or a least a comment explaining the situation.

Neither update_point_light_frusta nor update_spot_light_frusta feed off of `ComputedVisibility::is_visible()` (currently), but update_directional_light_frusta does. I'm guessing spot lights and point lights would also benefit from that, but id like to keep these changes as scoped as possible I think.
Definitely worth adding a comment though describing why the dependency exists.

This does make the component a slight bit bigger, and 14/16 bits go unused. Could we use a set of bitflags with a u8 underlying this? It would make the component remain as small as it is now.

Checking if a entity is fully visible is still a constant equality and setting each bit should still only be a single instruction on modern machines.
I experimented with this and didn't see any perf wins. I do have that listed in follow up work though (see the pr description). Happy to swap in bitflags if we have a compelling reason.
(probably after 0.8 at this point)
(reducing memory usage is a compelling reason!)
Memory usage is the primary one. Given how many visible entities there are, this would be a nice reduction.
